WANTED: A Salesperson With a Servant's Heart Who Picks Up the Phone Before Anyone Tells Them To
 Client Account Manager, Wealth Without Wall Street
 Most salespeople fall into one of two camps.
 The first camp can close, but clients feel like a number the minute the ink dries. 
 The second camp is lovely to talk to, but they won't ask for the business, and they let the phone sit there like it bites.
 We don't want either one. We want the rare person in the middle: someone who serves first, sells because they care, and dials without a second thought.
 Here's why. Over the years, thousands of business owners, investors and families have trusted Wealth Without Wall Street to help them build wealth outside the stock market. We do it with Infinite Banking (whole life insurance built for cash flow) and passive income education.
 Our strategists are very good at designing and placing policies. But once a policy is in force, too many of those clients go a long time without hearing from us. That's money left on the table. Worse, it's people left on their own.
 That's where you come in.
 The job, in plain English: You'll own a book of existing clients and past prospects. Your job is to call them, serve them, and grow the relationship into new business.
 You'll:
 Pick up the phone. A lot. Your day revolves around real conversations, not emails you hope get answered
 Re-engage clients who haven't heard from us in a while, and past prospects who didn't finish the process
 Run policy reviews, answer questions about policy loans and PUAs, and quarterback service so every client feels looked after. Our ops team handles the paperwork
 Uncover opportunities (new capital, a business sale, a growing family) and ask for the next step. Then book the client with one of our IBC strategists
 Ask every happy client for referrals, and follow up until they turn into conversations
 Introduce clients to our Passive Income Lab when it fits
 Spot clients drifting away and get on the phone before they leave
 Log every call and next step in HubSpot, and own your weekly numbers: contacts, opportunities, referrals, cases
 Who should NOT apply: Don't apply if you'd rather send a text than make a call. Skip this if asking for a referral makes you squirm. And if you see clients as commissions with names attached, this isn't your seat. Our clients can tell, and so can we.
 Who you are: 
 A servant first. You genuinely want your clients to win, and it shows in how you listen
 Phone-fearless. You'd rather have 50 real conversations than send 500 emails
 Not afraid to ask. You ask for the meeting, the next step and the referral, because you believe in what you're offering
 Relentless on follow-up. Nobody has to remind you, and nothing falls through the cracks
 Motivated by results. You like knowing your numbers and you like beating them
 What you bring: 
 2+ years in sales, account management or client relationships, ideally in insurance, financial services or wealth management
 A track record of hitting targets while keeping clients happy (bring examples)
 Comfortable on phone and video calls all day
 CRM discipline (HubSpot a plus)
 Active life insurance license, or willingness to get licensed within 60 days 
 Understanding of whole life insurance or Infinite Banking is a big plus. If you don't have it, we'll teach you
 How to apply (read carefully, because this is the first test): 
 You need to follow the application form below to a T, miss something you are not going to be considered. Attention to detail in this role is super imporant.
 Along with your résumé, we are going to ask for a short video talking about yourself, your sales background, your client services background and about a time you served a client so well that it turned into more business or a referral. Tell us what you did and what came of it.
 Bonus points in your video if you start it out with the words "Serve First" in the first line so we know you read this whole thing.
 Finalists will do a short Culture Index survey and a live role-play call . If phone calls make you nervous, this is where we'll find out.
 $40,000 - $50,000 base salary, so you have stability while you build
 Uncapped commission on every new case and referral you generate [8% of each case you originate, plus referral/Lab bonus]
 Warm conversations, not cold strangers. Every name in your book already knows who we are. Some already bought, and some almost did
 Our strategists handle the technical close, so you can focus on the relationship and the ask
 Paid licensing [if applicable] and full training on Infinite Banking, our service process and HubSpot
 A team that's growing fast, with a mission worth selling: helping families build wealth outside Wall Street
 Remote work

 What You'll Be Doing 
 Ads. You'll write new concepts and iterations based on the angles and customer profiles the Head of Paid Marketing sets. You write the scripts and the primary text. Each concept comes with a hypothesis, a target avatar, and your reasoning, and before you share it, you ask yourself one question: will this actually work? It's a high-volume role, with a steady flow of new concepts and iterations every week, scripted and briefed by Wednesday.
 Creative direction. You'll manage the video editors. You write the briefs and shot lists and show them what good looks like. They edit, and you make sure the final ad is right: pacing, the hook, captions, visuals, music, formats, and whether it still says what you wrote. You approve the final cut before it goes to review.  VSL and funnel copy. You'll write VSLs from the Head of Paid Marketing's brief, starting with a rewrite of the current one and then new VSLs for specific avatars. The company offers a full suite of simple, sophisticated financial products across managed investing, do-it-yourself trading, cryptocurrency, tax filing, spending and saving. Wealthsimple currently serves more than 4 million Canadians and holds over $155 billion in assets under administration. We're proud of what we've built — and we're just getting started. Read our Culture Manual https://www.wealthsimple.com/en-ca/culture and learn more about how we work https://www.wealthsimple.com/en-ca/careers.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Staff Product Manager to own Wealthsimple’s Connectivity Platform, spanning two critical areas:

 - Brokerage & Bank Linking: How clients securely and reliably connect external financial institutions to Wealthsimple.

 - Public API: How clients and partners securely access and use Wealthsimple financial data outside of Wealthsimple.



Together, these capabilities define how Wealthsimple connects to the broader financial ecosystem, and how every product team inside Wealthsimple builds on the external financial data that flows through it. This role will set the strategy for that platform and turn it into a reliable, scalable and differentiated capability for our clients, our product teams and our partners.



This is a platform role with a meaningful client experience surface. You’ll need to be equally comfortable thinking about APIs, data models and platform architecture as you are designing a client UX or deciding how Wealthsimple should work with an external provider.




ABOUT THE TEAM

The Brokerage & Bank Linking team builds the technology that lets clients link their outside bank and brokerage accounts to Wealthsimple. It owns the automated and manual linking experiences end to end, along with the three connectors behind them: Plaid, Flinks, and WST, our own in-house connector. That makes it one of the highest leverage surfaces in the company, and powers a growing set of experiences built by other product teams.




WHAT YOU’LL OWN

Connectivity Strategy

 - Set the long term vision and strategy for how Wealthsimple connects with the broader financial ecosystem.

 - Define the capabilities we should build ourselves, where we should rely on partners, and where we can create differentiated client value.

 - Develop a roadmap that balances immediate product needs with investments in reusable platform capabilities.

Brokerage & Bank Linking

 - Own the end to end experience for connecting external bank and brokerage accounts to Wealthsimple — automated and manual, including how clients recover when an automated connection fails.

 - Improve connection success, reliability and coverage across institutions, and own the routing strategy that decides which connector handles which institution and flow.

 - Own the client experience, including institution selection, authentication, errors, recovery and connection management.

 - Drive reliability and AI Powered  self-healing so connections detect and recover from failure without manual intervention.

 - Balance conversion against fraud exposure and operational load, making those tradeoffs deliberately with our risk and operations partners.

 - Develop the platform capabilities that allow Wealthsimple products to consume external financial data consistently.

 - Own relationships and product integrations with connectivity vendors such as Plaid and Flinks, and decide where our own connector should lead — including how much of the connector business Wealthsimple should be in long term and where it makes more sense to partner.

Public API

 - Own the strategy and roadmap for Wealthsimple’s Public API and external data connectivity.

 - Make it safe and easy for clients to permission their Wealthsimple financial data to the products and services they choose.

 - Define the platform capabilities required for authentication, consent, permissions, data access and partner integrations.

 - Identify and prioritize the partners and use cases that matter most to Wealthsimple clients.

 - Build toward a world where Wealthsimple is the financial institution where clients have the most control over their financial data.

 - Accelerate wealthsimple and our industry toward open banking.




SKILLS YOU BRING

You’re a strong product thinker who can operate across platform infrastructure, external ecosystems and client experience. You likely have:

 - Experience owning a platform, API, developer product or integrations platform, with a track record on metric-attached outcomes like conversion, success rate or reliability — not only feature delivery.

 - Enough technical depth to work closely with engineers on APIs, authentication, data models, routing and platform architecture.

 - Experience delivering through external vendors or partners whose roadmaps you don’t control, including making thoughtful build versus buy decisions and holding vendors accountable for product outcomes.

 - Comfort treating reliability as product work — error taxonomies, failure recovery, observability, and the operational load a product creates.

 - Experience weighing growth against fraud, risk and compliance, and holding both sides of that tradeoff.

 - The ability to turn a collection of technical capabilities into a clear product strategy and compelling long term vision, and to make the case for investing in it.

 - Strong analytical instincts and comfort using data to understand reliability, conversion, coverage and product performance, including building the measurement where it doesn’t exist yet.

 - Excellent cross functional leadership across Engineering, Design, Security, Legal, Compliance, Operations and external partners.

 - A bias toward simplifying complicated systems rather than layering more complexity on top of them.




NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience with open banking, Canada’s consumer-driven banking framework, or building to a data sharing standard

 - A background in financial data aggregation, whether at an aggregator, a bank, or a fintech consuming one

 - Experience shipping a public API or developer platform as a commercial product, including partner onboarding and support




WHAT GREAT LOOKS LIKE

You won’t just operate Bank Linking and ship API endpoints.



You’ll create a coherent connectivity strategy for Wealthsimple: making it easier for clients to bring their financial life to Wealthsimple, easier to move their financial data where they want it to go, easier for any team at Wealthsimple to build on that data, and increasingly less dependent on the slow pace of connectivity innovation from incumbent financial institutions.



You’ll also have made the case for what this platform should become — the metrics, the roadmap and the investment argument that get it there.

We specialize in leading-edge electronic product development, with hardware, embedded software, FPGA/ASIC, and signal integrity teams working together to design and deliver next-generation products for clients in emerging technology markets.
 Position Overview/Mandate: 
 The FPGA Designer plays a key role in designing and delivering complex FPGA-based systems for Fidus clients. You will work directly with customers and internal Fidus teams to define architectures, implement RTL, integrate IP, run simulations, close timing, and support lab bring-up and debug.
 This role is ideal for someone who enjoys working with new FPGA families and tools, is comfortable moving between different application domains (video, communications, storage, signal processing), and takes pride in producing high-quality, well-documented designs.
 Make an Impact with US: 
 At Fidus, you'll work on high-speed, high-complexity electronic systems, often using emerging technologies before they reach the broader market. You'll collaborate across FPGA/DSP, hardware, embedded software, verification, SI/PI, PCB layout, and mechanical/thermal design as part of cross-functional teams delivering real products for our clients.
 In practice, that means contributing to projects across Communications, Aerospace & Defence, Life Sciences & Medical Devices, Space & Satellite, Industrial Automation, Automotive, and Semiconductor engagements. You won't be limited to a single product or industry—your work will follow the technology, not just one roadmap.
 What You’ll Be Doing: 
 Work with our clients and other Fidus Employees to develop complex FPGA and/or CPLD based systems, including architecture, custom development, integrated IP, simulations, and timing analysis and closure.
 Design FPGA based systems using Xilinx and Intel based devices and tools
 Participate in design reviews (hardware-software interface, input-outputs etc.) to ensure Fidus quality standards and customer requirements are being adhered to
 Perform lab testing, debug of prototypes and supporting hardware/software engineer, as needed
 Perform customer prototype demonstrations and author test plans, design description and user documentation
 Provide technical insight to customers during the pre-sales and implementation phase of projects
 Provide technical support to the Business Manager and Sales team by providing detailed estimates on project scope, schedule, and deliverables and to present the technical aspects of Fidus proposals to the client
 Who You are: 
 Minimum 5 years of experience designing using RTL/Verilog/VHDL on FPGAs.
 Experience with video systems and specification standards, video algorithms, and high-speed memory and bus interfaces, communications protocols, and DSP or processor instantiations.
 Created designs using Xilinx or Altera FPGA families and have a solid understanding of tool flow
 Experience with Verilog, SystemVerilog, VHDL, Xilinx Vivado, Altera Quartus, and/or ModelSim
 RTL design and verification including test benches, functional simulations, and timing closure
 Exhibit strong communication skills, are fluent in English, have great customer interaction presence, and quickly learn new technologies and processes
 Proven techniques and habits that lead to high quality design
 Embraces AI as part of a modern engineering toolkit
 Degree as a B.A.Sc., B.Eng. or equivalent
 As AMD Embedded Premier Partner, you will be certified to highest level of FPGA qualification – this will be your first “to-do” item upon joining us.
 Location and travel: Position is based in Canada. Travel may be required domestically and internationally to support customer engagements and project delivery.
 This position may require access to export-controlled information. Candidates will be required to complete background checks and security screening under Canada's Controlled Goods Program (CGP) and may also be required to obtain a security clearance under the Contract Security Program (CSP) administered by Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC, formerly PWGSC).
 This role is an evergreen position.
 Annual base salary ranges from $125,000 to $160,000. The final offer within this range takes into account the variations in knowledge, skills, experience, and market conditions, and with consideration to internal equity.  
 Our competitive compensation package also includes a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision plans, matching GRSP contributions, annual profit-sharing bonus, along with other supplementary benefits.
 We also recognize that candidates show interest throughout different career stages and welcome all applications. When there is a great fit, the level of the role may be shifted as applicable. 
 About Fidus & Why Work Here 
 Since 2001, Fidus has completed over 4,000 projects for more than 400 customers across industries including Telecom/Datacom, Aerospace & Defence, Consumer, Semiconductors, Industrial/Automotive Controls, and Medical. As a Premier Adaptive Computing Partner for AMD North America, we combine deep technical expertise with industry-leading tools to solve complex design challenges.
 Fidus designs high-speed, high-complexity electronic systems using emerging technologies, often well before they reach the broader market. Our teams work across FPGA/DSP, hardware, embedded software, verification, SI/PI, PCB layout, and mechanical/thermal design to deliver real products for our customers.
 At Fidus, collaboration is at the core of how we work. We value openness, trust, and shared ownership, and we create an environment where people are encouraged to contribute ideas, learn from one another, and have a meaningful impact through the work they do.
 If all of this excites you, has your attention, and you can’t wait to join our amazing team and work environment, then we want to hear from you!
 Curious what it's actually like to work here? Take a look at our Working at Fidus page.
 Fidus has a commitment to ensure a fair and transparent recruitment process. Automated tools (including AI) support our initial screening of applicants against our job posting to identify candidates whose qualifications, experience, and skills align most closely with the position requirements. All further candidate assessments and final selection are conducted by our human recruitment team. AI does not make any final hiring decisions. 
 Thank you for your interest in Fidus. We welcome and encourage diverse candidates to apply. Accommodations are available upon request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process. Fidus is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer.

Job Description Summary 
Systems engineering is a cross-functional engineering discipline centered on an approach, mindset, and process. All activities that consider both the business and the technical needs of the customers with the goal of providing a quality product that meets the users needs. The discipline executes a robust process of design, creation, and optimization of systems, consisting of identification and quantification of system requirements, creation of alternate system design concepts, performance of design trade studies, selection and implementation of the best designs and verification that the design is properly integrated and executed. Process that proceeds from concept to production to operation. Impacts departmental operations and responsible for planning/execution. The role has some autonomy but is focused on execution of activities within an operating discipline covered by standard functional practices and procedures. Independent judgement is exercised on a regular basis. 
 Job Description 
 Essential Responsibilities: 
 Perform preliminary and detailed design of mechanical systems on the BWRX-300 including the steam turbine, turbine auxiliaries, main condenser, condensate, and feedwater systems
 Perform mechanical systems design and/or equipment procurement and construction activities, including requirements definition, process calculations and analysis, P&ID preparation, model review, vendor and client coordination, review and approval of vendor document submittals, and verification of deliverables produced by other engineers and teams
 Support the BWRX-300 certification processes for GE Products to address all US NRC (or other nuclear regulator) design certification requirements
 Conducts component and product integration. Participates in all activities that span multiple components, systems, and products and are concerned with how to integrate for maximum performance and operability. Manages product and systems requirements, specifications and flow down. Drives validation and verification activities for the overall product/system, including system level operability and testing. Responsible for defining product requirements for the module / component / subcontractors and partners teams. Manages interface between system and execution organizations.
 Responsible for driving CTQ / Risk trades within the teams designing the components. Manages the overall product configuration and configuration control system.
 Developing specialized knowledge in their system and discipline. Serves as best practice/quality resource. Has awareness of latest technical developments in own area. Contributes towards strategy and policy development and ensure delivery within area of responsibility.
 Have other duties as assigned by Manager
 Has in-depth knowledge of best practices and how own discipline and system integrates with others; has working knowledge of competition and the factors that differentiate them in the market
 Uses judgment to make decisions or solve moderately complex tasks or problems in areas of operational/product management, manufacturing, technology or engineering. Takes new perspective on existing solutions. Uses technical experience and expertise for data analysis to support recommendations. Uses multiple internal and limited external sources outside of own function to arrive at decisions.
 Acts as a resource for colleagues with less experience. May lead small projects with moderate risks and resource requirements. Explains difficult or sensitive information; works to build consensus. Developing persuasion skills required to influence others on topics within field.
 Interface with internal and external customers, suppliers, partners, licensing, the NRC and international regulatory authorities on technical issues
 Provide timely communications on significant issues or developments
 Required Qualifications: 
 Bachelor's degree in Mechanical or Nuclear Engineering
 Minimum 8 years of experience in an engineering role, with work in mechanical or process system design
 Minimum 2 years of experience in nuclear plant modifications, new construction, and/or nuclear fabrication, preferably with BWRs
 Minimum 4 years of experience in mechanical system design activities including development of process flow diagrams, thermodynamic and heat/fluid flow transfer calculations, engineering specifications, etc
 Eligibility Requirements: 
 Ability and willingness to travel up to 25%
 Desired Characteristics: 
 Master's degree in Mechanical or Nuclear Engineering
 Ability to effectively function in a dynamic design environment and manage the demands of multiple tasks and projects, while maintaining an uncompromised commitment to personal and nuclear safety principles
 Strong oral and written communication skills.
 Strong interpersonal and leadership skills.

 Who we are
 moneyGenius is a proudly Atlantic Canadian company with a simple mission: 
 Make money easy and fun for everyone. 
 To achieve this, we’re committed to making both moneyGenius.ca and creditcardGenius.ca the leading Canadian resources for all things money. In addition, we're reinventing personal finance education and rewards with our new GeniusCash app that makes learning about and maximizing your money fun and engaging.

These achievements are a testament to our growth, and reflect the remarkable hard work, dedication, and unwavering commitment of our team to our mission: to make money easy and fun for all Canadians. 
 So if you want in on our mission, read on…
 What you'll do
 We need an organized, detail-oriented Associate Editor who can write well-researched finance-focused stories, sharpen good content into something remarkable, manage our increasingly fast-paced editorial calendar, and keep things moving from idea to publication. In this role, you will:
 Manage a daily short-form content calendar, keeping topics and deadlines on track
 Brief content topics, with clear direction on audience, angle, and user experience
 Write well-researched personal finance content
 Edit content, polishing good work until every word tells and it's ready to publish
 Fact-check every piece for accuracy before it goes live
 Review all content through a reader's eye, making sure it flows as a cohesive whole and every link works
 Shape every story for a fun and memorable mobile app experience
 Refine editorial practices regularly, adapting to results like user engagement data
 Make sure every piece meets our Editorial Style Guide and quality standards
 Manage each piece of content end to end, following up until every task is closed
 Support stretch projects and cross-functional work as needed
 What it's really like working here
 We believe in being transparent about what this role entails – both the exciting parts and the challenges.
 You'll wear many hats in a lean startup environment . As a bootstrapped company, we don't have layers of specialized staff. Some days you'll be writing content from scratch; other days you'll be editing, fact-checking, planning the editorial calendar, or repurposing existing content. If you thrive on variety and get energized by tackling different challenges, you'll love it here. If you prefer a highly specialized role with a narrow set of responsibilities, this might not be the right fit.
 Quality and consistency are non-negotiable . We're a process-driven company because that's our competitive advantage. You'll need to follow our Editorial Style Guide and documented processes, and maintain meticulous attention to detail. We don't reinvent the wheel on recurring tasks – we perfect the process once and apply it consistently.
 We embrace experimentation and innovation . While we rely on our processes for repeat tasks, we also take on new challenges and are always evolving to respond to a changing content landscape. You’ll need to be ready to try new tools, measure your results, and adapt.
 Responsiveness matters deeply . We expect responses within hours on Zoom and within a business day by email. You'll need to close every communication loop by confirming completion or passing the ball to the next person. 
 Accountability is how we grow . When something goes wrong, we don't point fingers. We ask what we could have done differently and how we can capture those lessons into our processes. You'll be expected to take ownership of your work, proactively communicate when you need help, and deliver what you promised when you promised it.
 Fast-paced means really fast-paced . We're a lean team executing ambitious projects. Some weeks will be intense. You'll need to juggle multiple deadlines, think on your feet, and occasionally put in extra effort to get content out the door.
 The work matters . You're not just filling a content calendar – you're helping Canadians make better financial decisions. Your accuracy and high standards directly impact the trust our readers place in our brand.
 What makes it worth it
 You'll have real impact . In a small team, your contributions are visible and meaningful. You're not a cog in a machine – you're an essential part of making our mission happen.
 You'll grow fast . The variety of challenges and our commitment to evolution means you'll develop skills quickly, from writing and editing to managing custom content tools. We invest in our people because our success depends on your success.
 You'll work with people who care . Everyone here is committed to excellence and genuinely supports each other. We're building something meaningful together, and that creates a special team dynamic.

The IMO holds one integrated master plan, central value case objectives & realization, and a central view of program budget, setting the standards, decision gates, data and reporting that delivery teams work to. The IMO operates through a matrix of employees and consultants across the Bank, with the central programme office team and dedicated consultants reporting directly to the Vice President.
This is a cross-bank role. The Integration Management Office is the connective tissue between the Executive Leadership Team, the executive sponsors who own each workstream's outcomes, the Board and its committees, the Bank's regulators, and the vendor providing transition services. The Vice President sets the cadence, the control structure and the reporting spine those audiences rely on, and converts complexity into decisions and execution plans.
The role is deliberately broad rather than deep. Executive sponsors drive the substance within their own domains; the Vice President is accountable for the integrity of the whole across critical path, value case, risk management, and outcome accountability, including the judgment of when to verify, escalate, problem solve, or hold the line rather than absorb the work centrally.

Key Responsibilities - What You Will Lead: Own the integrated master plan and the critical path across every workstream, delivery organisation and partner, holding the baseline, the change control discipline and the monthly re-forecast.

 Own a single integration budget view across every workstream and initiative, making cost-to-complete a live number and carrying integration budget and value capture into the Financial planning cycles.
 Chair the funding pathway. Run the investment gate that tests both the business case and the readiness to execute before a recommendation reaches the Integration Steering Committee, and recommend funding approval only against approved scope, cost, value and design.

 Lead change management and people readiness for the combined bank, with change impact drawn from the same designs that drive the plan and employee readiness sequenced to customer conversion events rather than project milestones.

 Interlock with the business and technology delivery organisations so that capability, budget and resource stay aligned as work moves between them.

 Casual | Employee or Independent Contractor | Flexible Scheduling | Central Region 
 The Care Company is a home healthcare organization dedicated to creating A Better Life for Those at Home . We support clients of all ages to live safely, independently, and with dignity in the comfort of their own homes. Our mission is to help people Make Each Day Count by delivering exceptional, person-centred care that puts people first and strives to be Better Today than we were yesterday.
 We are seeking a passionate and experienced Physiotherapist (PT) to join our growing community rehabilitation team. This role is ideal for a Physiotherapist who enjoys the autonomy of managing their own community caseload while being supported by an experienced interdisciplinary team.
 This is a flexible, casual opportunity that can be structured as either an employee or independent contractor position , depending on the successful candidate's preference. Whether you are looking to supplement an existing caseload, build your community practice, transition into home care, or simply enjoy the flexibility of accepting referrals that fit your schedule, we would love to hear from you.
 You will work closely with clients and their families in the home, completing comprehensive assessments, developing individualized treatment plans, and implementing evidence-based interventions that improve mobility, strength, balance, endurance, and overall function. Many of the individuals we support are living with complex or chronic medical conditions and require Alternate Level of Care (ALC) services.
 This is an exciting opportunity to join The Care Company as we continue to build and expand our Physiotherapy program. Beyond delivering exceptional clinical care, there will be opportunities to contribute to new service development, Requests for Proposals (RFPs), quality improvement initiatives, and innovative models of care that can help expand Physiotherapy services across the community.

 Who This Role Is Perfect For
 This opportunity may be a great fit if you are:
 A Physiotherapist looking to supplement your existing caseload or private practice. 
 Interested in working as either an employee or independent contractor. 
 Looking for greater flexibility and autonomy over your schedule. 
 Passionate about helping clients remain mobile, safe, and independent in their homes. 
 Interested in mentorship, leadership, and supporting future Physiotherapists. 
 Entrepreneurial-minded and excited by the opportunity to help build and grow an evolving community rehabilitation program. 
 Comfortable working independently while knowing clinical and operational support is always available when needed. 
 What You'll Do
 As a Physiotherapist with The Care Company, you will have the opportunity to make a meaningful difference in clients' lives while enjoying the autonomy and flexibility of community practice. Working collaboratively with an interdisciplinary team, you will:
 Complete comprehensive in-home physiotherapy assessments within the required referral timeframe, including mobility assessments, balance evaluations, gait analysis, falls risk assessments, range of motion, strength testing, pain assessments, and functional mobility evaluations. 
 Develop individualized, evidence-based treatment plans that maximize mobility, independence, safety, and quality of life. 
 Provide follow-up visits focused on therapeutic exercise, gait training, balance retraining, mobility progression, pain management, post-operative rehabilitation, neurological rehabilitation, cardiorespiratory rehabilitation, and falls prevention. 
 Develop individualized home exercise programs and educate clients and caregivers to promote long-term success outside of treatment sessions. 
 Recommend and train clients in the safe use of mobility aids, gait aids, and assistive devices while collaborating with Occupational Therapists regarding equipment and home safety recommendations. 
 Support clients and families through education, coaching, and practical strategies that promote confidence, independence, and successful aging in place. 
 Collaborate closely with Occupational Therapists, nurses, Personal Support Workers, physicians, care coordinators, case managers, and Ontario Health atHome to support seamless care transitions. 
 Monitor client outcomes and modify treatment plans to ensure meaningful, measurable progress toward each client's rehabilitation goals. 
 Maintain accurate, timely, and clinically sound documentation. 
 Communicate proactively with the office regarding caseload availability, scheduling changes, urgent referrals, and client progress. 
 Independently manage your caseload and schedule while receiving administrative, scheduling, clinical, and technical support from The Care Company. 
 Deliver compassionate, ethical, and evidence-informed care while upholding The Care Company's commitment to clinical excellence. 
 Beyond Clinical Care
 This role offers more than a traditional community caseload. As The Care Company continues to expand its Physiotherapy services, you may also have opportunities to:
 Help shape and grow our community Physiotherapy program. 
 Contribute to new service development and Requests for Proposals (RFPs). 
 Participate in quality improvement initiatives and innovative models of community rehabilitation. 
 Mentor Physiotherapy students during community placements and help develop the next generation of Physiotherapists. 
 Support the onboarding and mentorship of future Physiotherapists joining the organization. 
 Collaborate with leadership on the development of clinical resources, treatment pathways, and best practices. 
 Grow into future clinical leadership and mentorship opportunities as our rehabilitation program continues to expand.

 Flexible, casual scheduling with no fixed weekly schedule.

 Ability to independently manage scheduling and communicate promptly with the office regarding availability. 
 Travel between client homes is required; access to a reliable vehicle is considered an asset.

 Registered and in good standing with the College of Physiotherapists of Ontario (CPO) . 
 Experience providing home and community care, particularly with HCCSS and/or Ontario Health atHome clients , is strongly preferred. 
 Community physiotherapy experience and/or hospital discharge, rehabilitation, or transitional care experience will also be considered. 
 Demonstrated skill in mobility assessments, falls prevention, gait training, balance retraining, therapeutic exercise prescription, neurological rehabilitation, orthopedic rehabilitation, and post-operative rehabilitation. 
 Experience prescribing mobility aids and collaborating with interdisciplinary teams. 
 Strong understanding of community discharge planning, mobility supports, caregiver education, and promoting aging in place. 
 Strong electronic documentation skills. 
 Experience coordinating with interdisciplinary teams and communicating with physicians and case managers. 
 Ability to work independently in the community and produce clear, timely, clinically appropriate documentation. 
 Valid driver's licence and access to reliable transportation, or the ability to travel efficiently within the designated service area. 
 Compensation
 $140 per initial assessment , including completion of the physiotherapy assessment, development of an individualized treatment plan, and any required funding applications or recommendations. 
 $75 per in-person follow-up visit. 
 $50 per virtual follow-up visit. 
 $25 per 30 minutes of approved administrative time completed outside of scheduled client visits, including documentation, care coordination, report writing, communication with physicians and interdisciplinary team members, development of home exercise programs, funding applications, equipment recommendations, and other client-related administrative duties. 
 We believe Physiotherapists should be fully compensated for the work they perform beyond direct client visits, recognizing that excellent community rehabilitation extends well beyond face-to-face treatment time.

 Flexible, casual scheduling – accept referrals based on your availability without being tied to a fixed weekly schedule.
 Autonomy to build and manage your own community caseload while being supported by an experienced interdisciplinary team.

 Mentorship opportunities with Physical Therapy students and future clinicians.
 Opportunities for future clinical leadership and program development.

 Educational training and ongoing professional development opportunities.
 PPE provided.

 Staff and service provider appreciation events.

About Faire 
 Faire is a technology wholesale platform built on the belief that the future is local. Independent retailers around the globe collectively represent a multi-hundred-billion-dollar wholesale market that has historically been fragmented and offline. At Faire, we're using the power of tech, data, and machine learning to connect this thriving community of entrepreneurs across the globe. Picture your favorite boutique in town — we help them discover the best products from around the world to sell in their stores. With the right tools and insights, we believe that we can level the playing field so businesses can grow and local communities can thrive.
 We’re looking for smart, resourceful and passionate people to join us as we power the shop local movement. If you believe in community, come join ours.
 About this role: 
 Our Engineering organization owns the software that makes our marketplace work. The Data Platform group supports everyone at Faire who depends on data: Product Engineering, Data Science, Machine Learning, Analytics, Strategy, Finance, and Product. Our job is to make sure the data is there, it's right, and people can find it and query it without having to think about the plumbing underneath.
 We are hiring a Staff Engineer to own that plumbing. Concretely, this means the path data takes out of our production databases (CockroachDB and MySQL) and into a place where analysts and data scientists can query it. Today that involves Fivetran, Kafka, Spark, and Airflow landing data in Snowflake and Databricks. It works, but it grew up over time and it shows. We want someone who can design the next version of it, build the hard parts personally, and bring the rest of the company along.
 This is a hands-on role. You'll also be the person other teams come to when they need to know how data should move at Faire.
 What you'll do: 
 Set the technical direction for how data moves from production systems into our analytical stores, and own the roadmap to get there over the next couple of years.
 Build the CDC and streaming ingestion layer: CockroachDB changefeeds and MySQL binlogs into Kafka, then into Iceberg tables on S3. You'll be responsible for the hard details like ordering, deduplication, late data, schema changes, and backfills.
 Implement data contracts and quality checks throughout our platform
 Put real ownership and SLAs on the datasets the business runs on, and wire quality checks into the platform with tools like Anomalo and Monte Carlo so we hear about broken data before a dashboard or a model does.
 Run Airflow and Fivetran well, and have an opinion about what we should keep buying versus what we should build.
 Own reliability for the platform: SLOs, on-call, incident reviews, and the follow-through so the same thing doesn't break twice.
 Work with the senior engineers, data scientists, and analysts who depend on this platform, and lead the migration of existing pipelines onto the new one without breaking what they rely on.
 Mentor the engineers around you. We want the team's data engineering practice to be better because you were here.
 Qualifications: 
 You've built and run data infrastructure that other teams depended on, at meaningful scale, and you've been the person setting direction for it, not just working on it.
 Deep experience with change data capture and streaming ingestion from operational databases through Kafka. You know what goes wrong with ordering, duplicates, snapshots, and schema evolution because you've dealt with it.
 Hands-on experience with lakehouse architectures on an open table format. Iceberg on S3 is what we use, so that's especially valuable. You should be comfortable talking about partitioning, compaction, catalogs, and copy-on-write versus merge-on-read.
 Strong Spark skills, and experience running Databricks and Snowflake against shared storage.
 Experience with data quality and observability in practice, including data contracts, SLAs, and tools like Anomalo or Monte Carlo.
 Experience operating Airflow at scale and working with managed ingestion like Fivetran.
 Strong SQL, and good instincts for how to model data so analysts and data scientists can actually use it.
 Solid Python plus at least one of Kotlin, Java, Scala, or Go. Experience shipping infrastructure on AWS with Terraform.
 A working understanding of data governance: access control, PII, retention and deletion, lineage, and audit.
 A track record of leading cross-team data initiatives and migrations, and of mentoring senior engineers.
 You can explain a technical tradeoff to a leadership team and to a new grad, and you can get people who disagree with each other to a decision.
 You take ownership of things that are broken or unowned, and you're willing to be on call for the systems you build.
 Experience in a marketplace, e-commerce, or other transaction-heavy business is a plus.
 Technologies we use and teach: 
 Python, Kotlin, SQL
 Kafka, Fivetran, Airflow
 S3, Apache Iceberg, Snowflake, Databricks, Apache Spark
 AWS, Terraform, Kubernetes
 CockroachDB, MySQL, Scylla and DynamoDB

 This role will also be eligible for equity and benefits. Actual base pay will be determined based on permissible factors such as transferable skills, work experience, market demands, and primary work location. The base pay range provided is subject to change and may be modified in the future.

Then Jobber might be the place for you. We’re looking for a Partner Marketing Manager to join our Product Marketing team and help shape and execute go-to-market programs across our technology and channel partner ecosystem.

Jobber exists to help people in small businesses be successful. We work with small home service businesses, like your local plumbers, painters, and landscapers, to transform the way service is delivered through technology. With Jobber they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers, while providing an easy and professional customer experience. Running a small business today isn’t like it used to be—the way we consume and deliver service is changing rapidly, technology is evolving, and customers expect more. That’s why we put the power and flexibility in their hands to run their businesses how, where, and when they want!

Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. Jobber has also been named on the Globe and Mail’s Canada’s Top Growing Companies list, and Deloitte Canada’s Technology Fast 50™, Enterprise Fast 15, and Technology Fast 500™ lists. With an Executive team that has over thirty years of industry experience of leading the way, we’ve come a long way from our first customer in 2011—but we’ve just scratched the surface of what we want to accomplish for our customers https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ahVf4AjYlh4.



The team:

At Jobber, we believe great software works better together. Small businesses rely on a growing ecosystem of tools to run and grow their businesses, and partnerships help connect those tools into a seamless customer experience.

The Partner Marketing function sits within Product Marketing and helps bring Jobber’s growing network of 1,000+ partners to market, including 100+ app integrations available through the Jobber App Marketplace, as well as franchise, referral, and association partners.

Through co-marketing and go-to-market programs, we help customers discover and adopt valuable partner solutions while driving integration adoption and partner-sourced growth.



The role:

As a Partner Marketing Manager at Jobber, you’ll own partner marketing programs that drive customer adoption, partner growth, and business impact across Jobber’s ecosystem.

While you’ll support partner marketing across Jobber’s ecosystem, a significant focus today is growing awareness and adoption of integrations available through the Jobber App Marketplace. You’ll collaborate with partners such as Google, Zapier, Gusto, The Home Depot, and others to bring joint initiatives to market, while also supporting franchise, referral, and association partnerships that contribute to customer acquisition, partner-sourced growth, and ecosystem expansion.

Success in this role means increasing integration adoption, driving partner-sourced revenue growth, and building scalable programs that strengthen Jobber’s partner ecosystem.



The Partner Marketing Manager will:

 - Develop and execute go-to-market strategies for partnership initiatives, including co-marketing campaigns, product launches, content, events, marketplace promotions, and demand generation programs.

 - Build and manage partner relationships, collaborating on joint marketing plans, co-marketing programs, and growth initiatives that create value for customers, partners, and Jobber.

 - Develop positioning, messaging, enablement resources, and go-to-market assets that clearly communicate the value of partner solutions and integrations.

 - Partner with teams across Product, Partnerships, Sales, Marketing, Enablement, and Design to bring partner initiatives to market and improve how customers discover and adopt partner solutions.

 - Gather customer, partner, competitive, and market insights to identify growth opportunities, inform strategy, and strengthen partner programs.

 - Own partner marketing performance metrics, including integration adoption, marketplace engagement, partner-sourced pipeline and revenue, and campaign performance, and use data to optimize programs and drive business impact.



To be successful you should have:

 - 4+ years of experience in partner marketing, product marketing, ecosystem marketing, or a related B2B SaaS go-to-market role.

 - Experience supporting go-to-market initiatives for technology integrations, platform ecosystems, app marketplaces, or strategic technology partnerships.

 - Proven track record of developing and executing co-marketing programs with external partners.

 - Strong positioning and messaging skills — you can translate integrations and partner solutions into clear, compelling customer value.

 - Experience building and executing integrated marketing campaigns across multiple channels.

 - Strong program management skills and the ability to manage multiple initiatives simultaneously.

 - Strong stakeholder and relationship management skills; you’re comfortable working cross-functionally and directly with external partners.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

 - Data-driven mindset — you use performance data and customer insights to guide decisions and improve outcomes.

 - Ability to work independently, stay organized, and move projects forward in a fast-paced environment.

 - Willingness to travel occasionally for partner events.

Nice to haves

 - Experience working at a SaaS platform where third-party integrations are a core part of the customer experience.

 - Experience supporting franchise networks, referral partner programs, associations, or other channel partnership models.

 - Familiarity with app marketplace ecosystems, partner portals, developer programs, or ecosystem growth strategies.

 - Experience with partner ecosystem tools (e.g. Crossbeam) and partner attribution methodologies.

 - Experience working in a fast-growing company.



Compensation:

At Jobber, we believe that compensation should be transparent, fair, and reflective of your experience and growth. This role has a minimum annual salary of $98,300, a midpoint of $115,700 and a maximum salary of $133,100, designed to show the progression from learning the ropes to truly excelling.

We design our compensation to reflect each new hire’s skills, experience against the complexity of the role, ensuring a fair and competitive salary. Our range is intentionally broad to support growth and long-term impact, with fully established hires typically starting around the midpoint. The higher end of the range is reserved for those who have demonstrated deep expertise and lasting contributions, while offers below the midpoint reflect strong potential with room to develop. This approach ensures that compensation aligns with both an individual’s current capabilities and their opportunity for future growth.

Base salary is just one part of a total compensation package that will include equity rewards, annual stipends for health and wellness, retirement savings matching, and an extended health package with fully paid premiums for body and mind. Your professional growth matters to us too! You’ll have access to a dedicated talent development program that includes career coaching and opportunities for career development.

We believe in transparency and open conversations about compensation. If you have any questions about our approach, we’re happy to discuss them throughout the hiring process!



Location:

We believe great collaboration is intentional, and sometimes that means coming together in person to build, brainstorm, and connect. To support this, the role is open to candidates based in one of our hub cities: Edmonton, Toronto, Vancouver, or Kitchener-Waterloo.

What you can expect from Jobber:

 - A dedicated Talent Development team and access to coaching, learning, and leadership programs to help you grow your career, reach your goals, and unlock your full potential.

 - To work with a group of people who are humble, supportive, and give a sh*t about our customers.

We believe that diverse teams perform better and that fostering an inclusive work environment is a key part of growing a successful team. We welcome people of diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we are committed to working with applicants requesting accommodation at any stage of the hiring process.

Job by job, we’re transforming the way service is delivered. Your lawn care provider, home cleaning service, plumber or painter could use Jobber to better connect with their customers, save time in the office, invoice faster, and get paid! We’re bringing tens of thousands of people together with technology to deliver billions of dollars a year in services to happy customers. Jobber exists to help make these small businesses successful, and when they’re successful we all win!

We are Paramount Commerce, a leading fintech company that has been simplifying payments in Canada since the early 2000s. We process $5 billion annually for some of the world's largest gaming and cryptocurrency platforms across Interac, EFT and soon to be RTR rails. Our infrastructure sits at the centre of how money moves in Canada.
 As we scale into new verticals and prepare for global expansion, the complexity of what we sell is outpacing the way we sell it. Our payment products span multiple rails, settlement models, and regulatory frameworks. The merchants buying them are increasingly sophisticated, with their own payments engineers and product teams who expect a technical counterpart on our side of the table. Today, that counterpart doesn't exist as a dedicated function. That's about to change.
The Opportunity
 Reporting directly to the CRO, you will serve as the connective tissue between our commercial goals and our technical capabilities. You’ll partner with a Product team focused on developer experience and an Engineering team that prizes robust infrastructure, ensuring our largest merchants in gaming and fintech receive a seamless, world-class onboarding experience from the very first meeting.
 You will be the first dedicated Solution Architect at Paramount Commerce. This is not a role where you inherit a playbook and run it. You will build the function, define how we engage with merchants technically, and become the person that Sales can't close a strategic deal without.
 The challenge is real: our deals involve merchants integrating across payment methods with different settlement flows, compliance constraints, and edge cases that surface late if nobody catches them early. When a gaming platform needs to understand how Interac request-to-pay works alongside their existing card acquiring setup, or a crypto exchange needs to map our A2A flows to their treasury architecture, you're the one in the room making it concrete.
 Right now, that work falls across Product, Engineering, Onboarding and Business Development in ways that slow deals down and create post-signature surprises. Your job is to own that space, eliminate the ambiguity, and make our technical sales process as strong as our infrastructure.
 What You'll Do
 Be the Technical Authority in the Room
 Join late-stage and strategic sales conversations where technical credibility wins or loses the deal. You're here to make sure deals close with full technical certainty so they succeed after signature, not just before it.
 Articulate how our payment solutions work, where they don't, and what it actually takes to integrate
 Structure solutions across payment methods (A2A, Interac, EFT), settlement flows, and compliance constraints
 Identify risks early and prevent deals from gaining complexity that kills them post-signature
 Translate Between Two Worlds
 Work directly with merchant-side product managers, payments engineers, and technical architects to understand their integration requirements and constraints. You become the trusted source of truth that both sides of the table rely on by documenting:
 Integration flows and technical architecture
 Edge cases and compliance dependencies
 Product gaps and required enhancements
 Own Technical Pre-Sales End to End
 Lead technical discovery, solution design, and integration scoping from first conversation through handoff to delivery. Over time, you'll build the repeatable assets that make this scalable:
 Solution templates by vertical (gaming, remittance, crypto, marketplace)
 Integration playbooks and technical qualification frameworks
 FAQs and objection-handling guides that reduce dependency on Product and Engineering for routine deal support
 Improve What Happens After the Signature
 Partner with implementation and engineering teams to ensure clean handoffs that reduce time-to-launch and eliminate avoidable rework. The best SE functions don't just close deals; they make deals successful.
 Ensure seamless Sales to Delivery transitions with complete technical context
 Identify recurring friction points and feed them back into product roadmap and commercial positioning
 Build the Function
 Define the engagement model between Solutions Engineering, Sales, Account Management, and Product. You're laying the foundation; make it strong enough to build on.
 Establish documentation standards and technical deal qualification criteria
 Create the processes and templates that let this function scale beyond you
 Shape what "good" looks like for Solutions Engineering at Paramount Commerce
What Success Looks Like
 First 6 Months
 Sales pulls you into every strategic deal because you've proven you change outcomes
 Post-signature technical surprises have dropped significantly because risks are identified during the sales cycle, not after
 You've produced the first set of vertical-specific solution templates that the commercial team actually uses
 Product receives structured, high-quality input on merchant requirements instead of secondhand notes from sales calls
 12 Months
 Integration timelines have measurably improved through better scoping and cleaner handoffs
 You've established a repeatable technical pre-sales process that doesn't depend on pulling engineers into sales calls
 The function has a clear roadmap for scaling, whether that means additional hires, better tooling, or both
 You have a direct and trusted relationship with the CRO, Product leadership, and Engineering leads
What You'll Bring
 Payments Depth, Not Surface Knowledge
 7 to 10+ years in Solutions Engineering, Sales Engineering, or a technical pre-sales hybrid within the payments industry. You understand the Canadian and US payments ecosystem at an operational level: Interac (e-Transfer, request-to-pay, and where real-time rails are headed), A2A and EFT flows, card acquiring, and the real distinctions between PSPs, processors, and gateways. You've seen enough payment integrations go sideways to know where the risk actually lives. Direct experience in gaming, crypto, or fintech integrations will put you at the top of the pile.
 Technical and Commercial Fluency
 You can discuss API authentication patterns with a merchant's engineering team and then walk into a commercial negotiation about settlement timing in the same meeting. You have a strong working knowledge of APIs, webhooks, reconciliation, and settlement flows. You simplify complexity without losing precision.
 Merchant-Side Credibility
 You've worked directly with product managers, engineers, and payments teams on the merchant side. You can handle deep technical questioning, navigate ambiguous requirements, and guide stakeholders who don't fully understand their own systems toward clarity. This is most of the job.
 Builder Mentality
 You've been the first or early SE hire before, or you've operated in an environment where you had to create process rather than follow it. You care about closing deals and making them succeed post-sale. You see inefficiency and fix it without waiting for permission.
Who This Role Is For
 This role is for someone who has spent years watching deals get complicated because nobody owned the technical narrative. You've seen the post-signature scramble when integration requirements weren't properly scoped, the engineering frustration when sales promises don't match technical reality, and the merchant churn that follows. You want to fix that, not just for one deal but structurally.
 You should be comfortable being the person who says "that won't work the way you think it will" in a room full of people who want to hear the opposite. You should be equally comfortable proposing the alternative that actually will. 
If you've been looking for a role where you build something from the ground up, have direct access to executive leadership, and work on problems that matter in a payments company that processes real volume, this is it.

Notre infrastructure est au cœur de la circulation monétaire au Canada.
 Alors que nous nous déployons dans de nouveaux secteurs verticaux et préparons notre expansion mondiale, la complexité de nos produits dépasse notre façon de les vendre. Nos solutions couvrent de multiples réseaux, modèles de règlement et cadres réglementaires. Les marchands qui les achètent sont de plus en plus sophistiqués; ils disposent de leurs propres ingénieurs de paiement et équipes produits qui s'attendent à avoir un homologue technique à la table de discussion. Aujourd'hui, cet homologue n'existe pas en tant que fonction dédiée. Cela est sur le point de changer.
 L'Opportunité
 Relevant directement du Chef des revenus (CRO), vous servirez de lien entre nos objectifs commerciaux et nos capacités techniques. Vous collaborerez avec une équipe Produit axée sur l'expérience développeur et une équipe d'Ingénierie qui privilégie une infrastructure robuste, garantissant ainsi à nos plus grands marchands (jeux et fintech) une expérience d'intégration fluide et de calibre mondial dès la première rencontre.

Lorsqu'une plateforme de jeux doit comprendre comment le "Demander un paiement" d'Interac fonctionne avec sa configuration d'acquisition de cartes actuelle, ou qu'une bourse de crypto doit mapper nos flux A2A à son architecture de trésorerie, c'est vous qui rendez le tout concret.

 FAQ et guides de gestion des objections pour réduire la dépendance envers les équipes Produit et Ingénierie.

 Assurer des transitions fluides entre les Ventes et la Livraison avec un contexte technique complet.

If that sounds like you, here’s your next big opportunity:
 AlgaeCal is searching for a top-tier Marketing Leader (Campaigns) to join our team and propel our revenue growth to new heights.
 Small print here ⇒ We’re an eCommerce company. So, we want you to have eCommerce experience. Lots of it. So if you don’t love digital marketing the way cats love cream, you probably shouldn’t read any further. 
 Still here? Okay then…
 This job will give you ALL the feels:
 At AlgaeCal, we’re driven by a single idea. To end the fear of bone loss. In the United States, an estimated 54 million people have low bone density. 
 The good news? AlgaeCal has the world’s only clinically-backed natural solution to this problem. We give hope to everyone worried about bone loss. If that excites you, you’ll find no better place to continue your career than at AlgaeCal. 
 This job might be for you if you’ve got…
 2+ years of marketing leadership experience planning and executing D2C campaigns in an eCommerce environment. You’ve led campaigns from the first messy idea through briefing, approvals, launch, optimization, reporting, and “okay, what did we learn?” You know campaigns don’t magically happen because someone made a promo calendar. They happen because someone owns the moving parts.
 A track record of managing six-figure monthly marketing budgets. You've worked with substantial media investments, understand how budget allocation impacts overall business performance, and know that maximizing profit matters more than simply maximizing spend.
 A Yoda-like ability to make strategic, data-driven decisions. When we look at your resume, we’ll see proof that you know how to turn campaign performance data into smart decisions. CPA, ROAS, revenue, customer segments, contribution margin, EBITDA - these numbers don’t make your eyes glaze over. They make your brain start whirring.
 A full-funnel brain that sees the whole customer journey. Paid media, email, ecommerce, loyalty, organic social, affiliates, influencers, customer service, marketplaces - you understand these channels don’t live in separate little kingdoms. They all touch the same customer. And if the journey feels disjointed, confusing, repetitive, or poorly timed, performance suffers.
 Strategy that converts like a tent revival. You’ve planned campaigns that engage, educate, and motivate people to take action. You understand offer strategy, timing, landing pages, upsells, cross-sells, bundles, coupons, discount logic, and the tiny campaign mechanics that can quietly make or break revenue. You know when evergreen ads, emails, popups, organic posts, or automations need to pause, shift, suppress, or get out of the way so a live campaign can do its job.
 A brain the size of a small planet! In this role, you’ll need to think imaginatively and act strategically. You’ll balance company priorities, finance approvals, product logistics, creative capacity, compliance, customer service needs, and channel constraints without melting into a puddle.
 A results-driven approach to paid media and campaign budget. You’ve worked closely with Paid Media teams, helped allocate spend across campaigns, and know how to look beyond surface-level ROAS. Revenue is nice. Profitability is nicer. You understand unit economics, contribution margin, and why a campaign can look good in one dashboard and less thrilling in another.
 A track record of leadership, mentorship, and cross-functional coordination. You’ve worked with channel owners, project managers, analysts, creatives, and senior leaders to get campaigns out the door without everyone needing therapy afterward. You guide, influence, pitch, negotiate, and push back when needed - without turning into a tiny workplace dictator.
 The ability to put on the Customer Hat at all times. You think through what a new prospect sees, what a returning customer receives, how reward points affect the offer, what happens if someone talks to Customer Service, and whether the whole experience actually makes sense to a real human being.
 Experience designing and executing customer journeys. From first click to final purchase, from campaign email to landing page, from retargeting ad to checkout, from BAU content to live promo, you know how to make every touchpoint feel connected, intentional, and easy to follow.
 A thick portfolio that demonstrates your mastery of all-things eCommerce. Sorry, but if you have to Google what a heatmap is, don’t know why site speed matters, or think an A/B test is just “trying a different headline,” this probably isn’t the job for you.
 A detective’s eye for revenue leakage. Coupon abuse, conflicting emails, poorly timed popups, expired offers, unclear bundles, bad suppression logic, clunky checkout journeys, ads running to the wrong page - you can spot the problems before they quietly drain sales.
 An encyclopedic knowledge of today’s martech, adtech, attribution, and analytics landscape. You don’t blindly trust one dashboard because it has a pretty graph. You understand tools like Triple Whale and GA4 can disagree, and you know how to contextualize performance instead of taking any single source as gospel.
 A strong grasp of testing strategy. A/B testing, multivariate testing, UX tests, offer tests, funnel tests, creative tests - you know how to plan tests that align with bigger roadmaps instead of throwing spaghetti at a wall and calling it “experimentation.”
 A solid understanding of UI/UX. This isn’t essential, but it’s a definite plus. You don’t need to be a designer, but you should understand how UX and UI choices affect customer behavior, conversion, trust, and campaign performance. And yes, we might swoon if you have it.
 A healthy respect for compliance, claims, and disclaimers. We work in the health space, which means “close enough” is not close enough. You’ll need to understand marketing claims, product basics, customer service considerations, and legal disclaimers well enough to keep campaigns accurate, compliant, and trustworthy.
